method_note: commons.wikimedia.org, en.wikipedia.org and api.wikimedia.org are all blocked by this sandbox's egress proxy for direct WebFetch. All Commons license text below was obtained via Firecrawl's indexed search snippets (mcp__Firecrawl__firecrawl_search, includeDomains=commons.wikimedia.org), which return literal excerpts of the rendered file page (including the 'Licensing' section text). Where a snippet directly quotes the file page's license/attribution text, confidence is 'verified'; where the license was only inferable from category listings, sister-wiki mirrors, or WebSearch's synthesized summary (not a literal on-page quote), confidence is 'indexed'. Direct-file URLs use the Commons 'Special:FilePath/<filename>' stable redirect when the literal upload.wikimedia.org hashed path was not captured in a snippet; where the hashed upload.wikimedia.org URL WAS captured verbatim, that is given instead and noted.

attribution_rules.source: creativecommons.org license deed pages, quoted verbatim via Firecrawl search snippets

CC_BY_SA_3.0.quoted_clause: Attribution — You must give appropriate credit, provide a link to the license, and indicate if changes were made. You may do so in any reasonable manner, but not in any way that suggests the licensor endorses you or your use.
CC_BY_SA_3.0.also_note: The by-sa/3.0 deed page also carries a notice: 'This is an older version of this license. Compared to previous ... [CC] strongly recommend the use of the 4.0 license instead.'

CC_BY_SA_4.0.quoted_clause: Attribution — You must give appropriate credit, provide a link to the license, and indicate if changes were made. You may do so in any reasonable manner, but not in any way that suggests the licensor endorses you or your use.

CC_BY_4.0.quoted_clause: Attribution — You must give appropriate credit, provide a link to the license, and indicate if changes were made. You may do so in any reasonable manner, but not in any way that suggests the licensor endorses you or your use.

TASL_best_practice.source: Creative Commons wiki 'Best practices for attribution', paraphrased by multiple library guides that quote it
TASL_best_practice.note: CC's recommended attribution formula is the acronym TASL: Title, Author, Source, License — i.e. name the work, name the creator, link to where it came from, and name/link the license. This is CC's stated best practice, not a strict legal requirement of the license text itself, but the credits page should follow it for every entry below.

attribution_rules.practical_rule_for_this_book: Every BY-SA (3.0 or 4.0) image being duotoned/cropped is a derivative work: the credits page must (1) name the original author/attribution string exactly as the file page states it, (2) link to the file's Commons page and to the CC license, (3) note that the image has been cropped/duotoned (adaptation), and (4) the adaptation itself must remain available under the same BY-SA license if the book redistributes the crop as a standalone file. CC BY (no SA) images (e.g. the Aumann, Robert (1930).jpg / David Orban photo, and CC BY 3.0 James C Scott photo) only require credit + link, no share-alike obligation on the crop.
